0. Verdict at a glance

Decision for finding-1
SeverityCountHeadline
CRITICAL1Cron-injected prompts almost-certainly fire UserPromptSubmit, so the WRITE hook resets last_user_input_epoch every 5 min. The idle clock never crosses 30 min, and presence-state never leaves active. Phase-1 fallback path becomes unreachable in production.
HIGH3(a) Documentation in both autonomous-fallback skill files still asserts "presence is unknown until phase 3, so step 4 always escalates" — that statement is now FALSE (server-API integration collapsed phase 3 into phase 1). (b) Presence-tracker SKILL.md doesn't specify a curl --max-time — a hung server will hang every approval decision indefinitely. (c) Catastrophic Python exceptions in the WRITE hook can return a non-zero exit code, which by Claude Code semantics may BLOCK the user's prompt.
MEDIUM4Override-file malformed-YAML behaviour unspecified; "last recorded state" lookup mechanism for transition-log unspecified; presence-tracker called twice per decision (persona + skill); compaction-guard relies on model behavioural judgment instead of a deterministic marker.

STRENGTHS—Server-clock anchoring, R6 v3 enforcement at composition time, snapshot-rule on matrix read, fail-soft hook design, hard-floor as a separate gate before the matrix.

The CRITICAL finding is the only one that changes whether phase-1 actually does anything in production. The HIGH-(a) finding is documentation drift but it is the kind of drift that misleads future readers (and the model itself) about what the gate currently does. Everything else is hardening.

1. WRITE side — `scripts/amama_user_prompt_submit.py` + `hooks/hooks.json`

Decision for finding-2

Purpose. On every UserPromptSubmit, fire-and-forget POST to /api/sessions/me/user-input so the AI Maestro server can stamp last_user_input_epoch = server_clock_now for this AID owner.

1.1 CRITICAL — Cron-injected prompts treated as user input

File: scripts/amama_user_prompt_submit.py:34-49 Hook: hooks/hooks.json:17-28 (UserPromptSubmit)

The script unconditionally drains stdin and POSTs:

def _entry() -> None:
    try:
        sys.stdin.read()           # drained, never inspected
    except OSError:
        pass

    api_base = os.environ.get("AIMAESTRO_API", "http://localhost:23000")
    aid_auth = os.environ.get("AID_AUTH", "")

    if not aid_auth:
        return
    ...
    subprocess.run([... POST ...])

UserPromptSubmit fires on every prompt the REPL receives, including CronCreate-injected prompts (the janitor heartbeat, [janitor-renew], the /janitor-arm and /amama-* slash commands the user types, and any other system-injected turn). The ai-maestro-janitor plugin is currently armed at /5 * (heartbeat 0067b3ae, durable, recurring), so the script will POST every 5 minutes regardless of whether the human is at the keyboard.

Consequence. server_now_epoch − last_user_input_epoch never exceeds ~5 minutes for any AMAMA session that has the janitor armed. The state classifier in references/state-thresholds.md therefore returns active forever, and the persona's "When state ≠ active" decision tree never enters its non-trivial branches. Phase-1's fallback machinery is wired but unreachable.

This is exactly the failure mode that the server-clock anchoring fix (B8 / G6) was supposed to make irrelevant — but the input layer is poisoned before the server clock ever gets a chance to disagree.

Empirical caveat. I cannot confirm via reading alone that cron-injected prompts trigger UserPromptSubmit in the running Claude Code build. Two pieces of indirect evidence make it the strongly likely case:

  • The plugin's dispatch.sh is described as "each cron fire is a fresh user turn" — a "fresh user turn" is the exact event class UserPromptSubmit listens for.
  • This conversation has been receiving [janitor-heartbeat] messages as user-message turns; if they ride the same channel that hooks tap, the hook fires.

Suggested fix. Read the stdin payload (which is JSON for hook events), parse prompt, and short-circuit if the prompt starts with one of the known system-prefixes:

import json
raw = sys.stdin.read() or ""
try:
    payload = json.loads(raw)
    prompt = (payload.get("prompt") or "").lstrip()
except (ValueError, AttributeError):
    prompt = ""

# System-injected turns must NOT count as user input.
SYSTEM_PREFIXES = ("[janitor-heartbeat]", "[janitor-renew]",
                   "[janitor-resume]", "[janitor-")
if any(prompt.startswith(p) for p in SYSTEM_PREFIXES):
    return

The exact prefix list belongs in a constant at the top of the file with a short comment pointing at the upstream source (the janitor plugin's heartbeat skill defines them). Slash-command turns (/janitor-arm, /amama-...) are a judgment call — they are clearly USER actions, but they are not the human "leaning on the keyboard" signal the matrix wants to detect. Probably correct to count them.

Verification recipe (once empirical access is restored).

  1. Arm janitor at 5-min interval, leave the session idle 90 minutes, query GET /api/users/me/presence. If last_user_input_epoch is within the last 5 minutes, the bug is real.
  2. After applying the fix, repeat. last_user_input_epoch should match the timestamp of the LAST genuine user prompt.

1.2 HIGH — Catastrophic exceptions can block prompt submission

File: scripts/amama_user_prompt_submit.py:38-73

The narrow except catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired, subprocess.SubprocessError, FileNotFoundError, OSError. Anything else (MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, a malformed AIMAESTRO_API that breaks rstrip — unlikely but possible if the env var is set to a non-string somehow, an import-time failure if subprocess is shadowed, …) propagates out of _entry(), bubbles to the script's top level, and exits with a non-zero return code.

UserPromptSubmit is one of the hook events for which a non-zero exit can be interpreted by Claude Code as "abort this prompt". The script's docstring claims fail-soft, but the implementation only fail-softs the predicted error classes. This contradicts the comment at line 75: *"Always exit 0 — never block prompt submission on a presence-write failure."*

Suggested fix. Wrap the entire __main__ block in `try / except BaseException and force sys.exit(0)`:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        _entry()
    except BaseException:
        # Fail-soft is absolute — even MemoryError must not block input.
        pass
    sys.exit(0)

BaseException rather than Exception because the docstring promises ZERO blocking, and that includes KeyboardInterrupt mid-curl (unrealistic but cheap to defend against).

1.3 LOW — Content-Type header omitted

File: scripts/amama_user_prompt_submit.py:60-65

The POST sets Content-Length: 0 but no Content-Type. Most servers tolerate this for empty bodies, but strict body-parsers (e.g. Express with body-parser.json({strict: true})) sometimes return 415 instead of treating the body as empty. The server contract in design/handoffs/aimaestro-server-presence-api.md:8-15 says the body is empty, so this is server-team responsibility — but a defensive -H "Content-Type: application/json" is a one-line insurance policy.

1.4 NIT — No diagnostic channel

capture_output=True discards stderr. When debugging "why did the presence read say unknown" the answer often lives in curl's stderr (Could not resolve host, Connection refused, 401 Unauthorized). A best-effort append to ~/.aimaestro/amama-presence-write.log with exit-code + first 200 chars of stderr would pay for itself the first time something goes wrong. Optional.

1.5 NIT — Coverage gap: only AMAMA's session writes

Already flagged in the v2.9.0 ship summary. Documented here for completeness: a user who replies to a notification surfaced by a programmer/COS/MAINTAINER session does not update last_user_input_epoch, because those sessions don't ship the amama_user_prompt_submit.py hook. The matrix may classify the user as away while they are typing into a non-AMAMA window. R6 v3 makes this less common in practice (MANAGER is sole user interface), but the 1-edge reply-only paths still let other agents receive user input. Spread the WRITE hook (or a slimmed-down variant) to the COS / AUTONOMOUS / MAINTAINER / programmer / integrator role plugins.

2. READ side — `skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md`

Decision for finding-3

2.1 HIGH — No curl timeout specified

File: skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md:30

GET /api/users/me/presence with Authorization: Bearer $AID_AUTH.
If HTTP error or transport failure, return `("unknown", now,
"presence-api-unreachable")`.

The skill instruction does NOT specify how the model issues this GET. The natural implementation is `curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $AID_AUTH" $URL. Without --max-time`, curl uses its default connect-timeout (~120s) and no read-timeout. A hung server (or a slow network) will block the entire approval-decision turn.

The WRITE hook explicitly uses --max-time 2 (amama_user_prompt_submit.py:64). The READ skill should match. Recommend updating step 3 to read:

3. Presence read. GET /api/users/me/presence with
Authorization: Bearer $AID_AUTH **and a 2-second timeout
(curl --max-time 2)**. If HTTP error, transport failure, or
timeout, return ("unknown", now, "presence-api-unreachable").

This is the kind of detail the model will get right ~80% of the time without the explicit instruction; making it explicit closes that gap.

2.2 MEDIUM — Override-file malformed-YAML fallback unspecified

File: skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md:27 (step 2) Reference: references/state-thresholds.md:32-41

Step 2 says "If override carries a non-expired override, return …" — but does not specify what happens when the file exists but is malformed (corrupt YAML, missing state: key, missing expires_at:, expires_at in the past in a different timezone format than expected, etc.).

Phase-1 must fail-soft to "no override → continue to step 3". State the rule explicitly. Recommended additions:

  • Parse error → treat as "no override" (and stderr-warn).
  • Missing expires_at → treat as "no override" (defensive default; alternative is "permanent override" but that's a footgun).
  • expires_at in the past → treat as "no override".
  • state not in {active, monitoring, away, dnd, unknown} → treat as "no override".

The intent is that a hand-edited/garbage override file can never make AMAMA refuse to escalate when it should escalate, and can never lock AMAMA into auto-approval mode permanently.

2.3 MEDIUM — "Last recorded state" lookup is unspecified

File: skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md:33 (step 7)

7. Audit log on transition. Append one row when computed state
differs from last recorded.

How does the skill know the "last recorded" state? Three plausible implementations:

  1. Read the last data row of docs_dev/sessions/availability-log.md and parse the state column. Requires a stable row format; the format is not pinned in the SKILL.
  2. Keep an in-process variable that survives across calls within one Claude session. Loses the value across sessions and across compactions.
  3. Cache in CozoDB. Phase-1 spec defers CozoDB integration (TRDD §3.1 "phase 2 will add the formal availability_transitions schema").

Phase-1 lands with option 1 implicitly. The SKILL should pin the row format (e.g. a markdown table with `| timestamp | state | source | since |` columns) so the parse is reliable across sessions. Otherwise the model invents a slightly different format every time and "last recorded" becomes brittle.

If the model can't determine the last state, the safe default is "log the row anyway, even if it's a duplicate" — the audit log is an append-only artefact and a duplicate row is harmless. State this explicitly so the failure mode is "noise" rather than "silent gap".

2.4 MEDIUM — Compaction-guard relies on model judgment, not a marker

File: skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md:26 (step 1)

1. Compaction guard. If this is the first user-facing turn after a
detected compaction, return `("unknown-after-compaction", now,
"compaction-guard")` and stop.

"detected compaction" is a behavioural cue — the model is expected to remember that the prior <system-reminder> mentioned a compaction and to behave differently on the next turn. There is no on-disk marker, no hook, no env-var.

Claude Code DOES fire a SessionStart:compact hook (we observed it in this very session — the janitor reminder banner was the proof). That hook could write an atomic marker file:

$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/amama/last-compaction-at.ts

Then step 1 of the skill becomes deterministic: read the marker, compare to the timestamp of the previous successful presence read (cached in the skill's transition log), and if marker > previous-read, return unknown-after-compaction. The marker is then cleared by the next successful read.

This is a phase-1 hardening — non-blocking but worth queueing.

2.5 NIT — since semantics differ across return paths

File: skills/amama-presence-tracker/SKILL.md:26-32 (steps 1-5)

The same return tuple slot since is used for:

  • compaction-guard → now
  • override → override.since (e.g. when the override was set, possibly hours ago)
  • API unreachable → now
  • no input recorded → now
  • auto-clock → last_user_input_epoch

Callers that interpret since as "the moment when this state began" will be confused: for override it is when the override started; for auto-clock it is the moment the user last typed; for unknown it is "now" (which is the moment of failure, not the moment of state-onset). This is fine if all callers treat since as "best-effort hint, not a precise event time", but the SKILL should say so. One line under the Output section is enough.

3. Decision side — `skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/`

Decision for finding-4

3.1 HIGH — Doc says "phase 3 is when this becomes active" but phase 3 was collapsed into phase 1

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/SKILL.md:37

Phase-1 behavior: amama-presence-tracker returns unknown until phase
3 ships, so step 4 always escalates. Policy is wired but dormant.

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/decision-flow.md:32

Phase 1 default: state is always unknown until phase 3 ships, so
this gate fires for every request — by design.

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/decision-flow.md:92-94

## Phase-1 invisibility property
Steps 1-3 fire for every request. Step 4 (presence gate) ALWAYS
escalates in phase 1 because amama-presence-tracker returns unknown
until phase 3 ships. Therefore steps 5-10 don't execute in production
until phase 3 — they're wired but dormant.

This was true in the original v3 plan (where a separate PRESENCE plugin was supposed to ship in phase 3 and write the host-global ~/.aimaestro/host-state/last-user-input.ts file). It is FALSE after the v2.9.0 architectural pivot, which used the AI Maestro server's REST endpoints instead — collapsing phase 3 into phase 1. The presence tracker now returns concrete active|monitoring|away|dnd states whenever the API responds.

The model reading these files in a future session will believe the fallback path is dormant and act conservatively, OR be confused when it observes a non-unknown state and the documentation says that should be impossible. Both are bad failure modes.

Suggested rewrite (one paragraph in each file):

Phase-1 status (post 2026-05-06 server-API integration): the
presence-tracker now queries GET /api/users/me/presence and returns
concrete states whenever the server is reachable. Step 4 of this
skill therefore executes its full classification logic in production,
NOT a constant unknown. The earlier "phase 1 invisible until phase 3"
property no longer holds — phase 3 was collapsed into phase 1 by the
server-API pivot. What is still deferred to later phases: the
ratification ritual (phase 2), the HMAC cue protocol (phase 1.5), and
the multi-team fleet view (phase 4).

The TRDD (design/tasks/TRDD-bfcedff0-…md) also still describes the old architecture (TRDD §2, §3.1) and should be amended in lockstep. Suggest a TRDD-bfcedff0-amendment-2026-05-06.md change-log entry so the historical record stays clean.

3.2 MEDIUM — Presence is consulted twice per decision

File: agents/ai-maestro-assistant-manager-agent-main-agent.md:310 (persona step 1) File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/decision-flow.md:30-33 (skill step 4)

The persona's "When state ≠ active" decision tree calls amama-presence-tracker.get_state() (step 1), and so does the fallback skill (step 4). Two API roundtrips per approval decision, two opportunities for the server to be slow.

Defense-in-depth justification exists ("the skill must not rely on the caller having checked"), but the cost is real. Two cheap fixes:

  • Make decide(request) accept an optional state parameter: if supplied, skill uses it; otherwise skill calls get_state() itself. Persona passes the value it already computed.
  • Or: cache the last get_state() result in-process for ~10 seconds (turn-scoped). Server-side last_user_input_epoch doesn't change meaningfully on a 10-second timescale.

Either is a NIT-with-bite — works fine without it, but a 4-second worst-case approval latency is annoying for routine REVERSIBLE ops.

3.3 LOW — Hard-floor reference is off-by-a-few

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/SKILL.md:20

The hard-floor list at amama-amcos-coordination/references/delegation-rules.md:112-126 accessible.

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/reversibility-matrix.md:13

see amama-amcos-coordination/references/delegation-rules.md:112-126

Actual location of the seven-row hard-floor table in delegation-rules.md is lines 117-125 (the section header is at line 109, the table itself spans 117-125 in the current file — re-checked just now: file is 126 lines total, table is the last block). The cited range "112-126" is close but not precise; future readers running sed -n '112,126p' on the file will get a few lines of preamble plus the table.

Trivial fix — just update the line range. Or, better, drop the line range entirely and cite `## 4. Operations That ALWAYS Require AMAMA Approval` (the section header) since that survives line-shift edits.

3.4 LOW — Phase-1 string-match guard regex is too narrow

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/decision-flow.md:24

regex (production|prod|main|secrets|credentials|iam|auth)
(case-insensitive)

This is intentionally over-broad on the documented intent ("accepts false positives in exchange for safety"), BUT it misses some obvious high-risk substrings:

  • migration (DB migrations are hard-floor row 22 territory)
  • deploy / release (covers row 19/20 even when "prod" is not in the branch name)
  • master (still common alongside main)
  • password / key / token (cover credentials in fields named differently from secrets)

Phase-1 string-match is replaced by HMAC in 1.5, so this only matters for the few weeks/months that 1.5 takes to ship. Cheap to broaden.

3.5 NIT — Audit-log path lives in docs_dev/ (gitignored)

File: skills/amama-autonomous-fallback/references/decision-flow.md:67

docs_dev/approvals/autonomous-decisions-pending-ratification.md

docs_dev/ is gitignored (per project CLAUDE.md). Phase-2's ratification ritual (the next phase) consumes this log. The user has committed to "never delete _dev folder content", but the log is not backed up by git, not synced across machines, and disappears if the folder is rm-rf'd by mistake. For a load-bearing audit trail, consider moving it to a tracked location (e.g. design/audit/…) or having phase-2's ritual ALSO commit the file post-ratification.

This is a phase-2 concern, not phase-1, but worth flagging now while the path is being used by exactly one skill.

4. Persona — `agents/ai-maestro-assistant-manager-agent-main-agent.md`

Decision for finding-5

4.1 R6 v3 narrowing — solid

The three places R6 v3 is enforced (Communication Rules C5 at line 99-110, Communication Rules Summary at 363-371, Communication Permissions table at 654-689) are internally consistent. The "forbidden" verdict is repeated in three independent ways — table cell, prose paragraph, and "MANDATORY chain" sentence — which is the right amount of redundancy for a hard rule.

The empirical motivation paragraph (line 689) is a good documentation move: future readers (and the model) understand WHY the rule exists, not just what it says.

4.2 "When state ≠ active" decision tree — generally clean

File: lines 306-319

The decision tree is well-ordered:

  1. Presence first.
  2. Fallback on monitoring/away/dnd.
  3. Verdict application with R6 v3 routing constraint inlined in sub-step 3.
  4. Hard-floor as a parallel always-true gate.
  5. Explicit "no cue parsing in phase 1" defence against prompt injection.

Two small nudges:

  • Step 1 wording. "If state is active, unknown, or unknown-after-compaction, escalate to user as today." Current wording is correct, but "as today" implies "this is what you used to do before phase 1" — that nuance is lost on a fresh model. Safer: "fall through to the existing approval flow, which always escalates to the user."
  • Step 5 footnote. The "no cue parsing in phase 1" defence is important. It deserves a reference to where cue parsing WILL ship (phase 1.5 with HMAC) — currently the reader has no pointer to the next step in the design.

4.3 Skills frontmatter — present

Lines 14-15 register both new skills. Confirmed.

5. Server contract — `design/handoffs/aimaestro-server-presence-api.md`

Decision for finding-6

5.1 Contract is appropriately tight

50 lines, two endpoints, one nullable field. No scope creep. The server_now_epoch co-return is the load-bearing design choice — it makes client-server clock skew structurally impossible, closing crisis B8.

5.2 LOW — A few corner cases not pinned

QuestionSpec answerRecommendation
What does GET return when the user record itself doesn't exist (first call ever)?Implied: 200 with last_user_input_epoch: null. Not stated.One sentence under "Response 200".
What does GET return on rate-limit?Not stated.Either 429 or never (state explicitly).
Does POST require Content-Type?Not stated.Empty body / no Content-Type required (matches what client sends).
Server clock backwards-jump (NTP correction): can server_now_epoch < last_user_input_epoch?Mentioned in the SKILL's max(0, …) clamp but not in the spec.Spec should state "server guarantees server_now_epoch ≥ last_user_input_epoch" so the clamp is a belt, not a brace.

7. Strengths worth preserving

Decision for finding-8
  • Server-clock anchoring (presence-tracker SKILL.md:30, state-thresholds.md §"Server-clock anchored idle computation"). The decision to return both last_user_input_epoch and server_now_epoch in the SAME response is the correct fix for crisis B8 — the client never has to reason about its own clock.
  • R6 v3 routing constraint enforcement at composition time (reversibility-matrix.md:65, decision-flow.md:46, persona:104-110). Whitelist-based recipient check makes the rule a protocol-level invariant rather than a behavioural guideline.
  • Snapshot rule on matrix read (decision-flow.md:50-52). Closes crisis F5 (concurrent edit during decision) without requiring a mutex.
  • Hard-floor as a separate gate before the matrix (SKILL.md:25-26, decision-flow.md:18-20). Belt-and-suspenders: even if the matrix is mis-edited and a row that should be W becomes R, the seven hard-floor categories still fire.
  • Fail-soft hook design (despite finding 1.2). Predicted error classes are caught explicitly; the design intent is correct, only the catch list needs broadening.
  • No cue parsing in phase 1 (persona:317). Closes the prompt injection vector that an HMAC-less cue would otherwise create.

8. Recommended fix order

Decision for finding-9

The CRITICAL-first ordering matches blast-radius. Items in [] are optional follow-ups.

  1. (CRITICAL) Patch amama_user_prompt_submit.py to skip system-prefixed prompts. (~10 LoC + a comment.) This unblocks the entire phase-1 architecture in production.
  2. (HIGH 1.2) Wrap the hook's __main__ in a BaseException-catching try/except + explicit sys.exit(0). (~5 LoC.)
  3. (HIGH 2.1) Add curl --max-time 2 to presence-tracker step 3. (Doc-only edit.)
  4. (HIGH 3.1) Rewrite the "phase 3 is when this becomes active" passages in autonomous-fallback/SKILL.md, decision-flow.md (×2 places), and the TRDD's §2 deferred-table. (Doc-only edits, ~20 LoC.)
  5. (MEDIUM 2.2) Spell out the override-file fail-soft contract. (Doc-only.)
  6. (MEDIUM 2.3) Pin the audit-log row format used to determine "last recorded state". (Doc-only.)
  7. (MEDIUM 2.4) Optional: add a SessionStart:compact hook that writes a last-compaction-at.ts marker; have presence-tracker step 1 check it. (~30 LoC + doc.)
  8. (MEDIUM 3.2) Optional: thread state from persona to skill, OR add a turn-scoped cache in presence-tracker. (~15 LoC.)
  9. (LOW) Items 1.3, 3.3, 3.4, 5.2 — small doc/code tweaks, batch into one cleanup commit.
  10. (NIT) Items 1.4, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.2 — schedule with phase 1.5 or phase 2 since they depend on those phases anyway.

If the user wants ONE fix tonight, it is item 1. Without it, phase-1's autonomous-fallback path is unreachable in production — which is also the safest possible failure mode (everything escalates), but it makes phase-1 a no-op from the user's standpoint.
